Do not plan modifications to files you have not actually looked at.\n\n#### Find related code patterns\n\nUse `Grep` and `Read` aggressively \u2014 pi-coding-agent does not have LSP or Serena, so text search is your primary tool:\n\n- **Literal symbol search**: `Grep` for the specific class/function/component names mentioned in the issue.\n- **Usage-site discovery**: `Grep` for imports of the target symbol to see who depends on it \u2014 e.g. `from \"../lib/graph-node-actions\"` finds every caller of that module.\n- **Pattern search**: find existing similar features to model after. If the issue asks for a new API endpoint, grep for `@Post(`, `router.post(`, or equivalent to find peer endpoints. If it asks for a new component, grep for peer component filenames.\n- **Test patterns**: look at how similar features are tested (`**/*.test.ts`, `__tests__/`) \u2014 the new work should match.\n\n**Example-driven analysis.** If adding an endpoint, find the nearest existing endpoint and study its structure, DI, error handling, and tests. If adding a UI component, find a similar one. **Study the pattern; do not reinvent it.**\n\n#### Dependency and integration analysis\n\n- Which modules will need changes? Which are read-only references?\n- Are there API contracts that cross module boundaries? Flag them.\n- Are there test files that will need updating alongside the source changes?\n- Are there shared types or utilities that need extending vs. duplicating?\n\n#### Output of Phase 2\n\nBy the end of Phase 2 you should have a concrete list of:\n\n- **Affected files** (with rationale for each)\n- **Patterns to follow** (with file:line references to the exemplar code)\n- **Cross-cutting concerns** (shared utilities, types, tests)\n- **Open questions** about scope, approach, or unclear requirements\n\n---\n\n### Phase 3: Implementation Approach Design\n\n#### Break down into atomic, committable tasks\n\nEach task should be one commit, independently reviewable. This is the core discipline of a good scratchpad.\n\n**Good task breakdown example:**\n\n```markdown\n- [ ] Add database schema for new entity\n  - Files: migrations/002_add_entity.sql, src/models/entity.ts\n  - Why: Foundation for feature, no dependencies on other tasks\n  - Testing: Unit tests for model validation in src/models/__tests__/entity.test.ts\n\n- [ ] Implement repository methods\n  - Files: src/repositories/entity-repository.ts, src/repositories/__tests__/entity-repository.test.ts\n  - Why: Data access layer \u2014 depends on the schema task above\n  - Testing: Repository integration tests against sqlite in-memory\n\n- [ ] Add REST endpoint\n  - Files: src/routes/entity.ts, src/controllers/entity-controller.ts\n  - Why: Expose functionality \u2014 depends on repository task above\n  - Testing: API endpoint tests in e2e/\n```\n\n**Bad task breakdown (avoid):**\n\n```markdown\n\u274c - [ ] Implement the feature         \u2014 too large, not atomic, not a commit\n\u274c - [ ] Add files                     \u2014 vague, no rationale\n\u274c - [ ] Fix bugs and add tests        \u2014 mixes concerns across commits\n\u274c - [ ] Refactor to use new pattern   \u2014 scope creep, unrelated to the issue\n```\n\n#### Task anatomy\n\nEvery task must specify:\n\n- **Files affected**: concrete paths, not \"the relevant files\"\n- **Why**: purpose and dependencies \u2014 what does this commit accomplish, and what does it depend on?\n- **Implementation notes** (optional): key decisions, approaches, or gotchas\n- **Testing**: what tests to write or update\n\n#### Ordering strategy\n\nOrder tasks by dependency, not by how natural they feel to write:\n\n1. **Foundation**: schemas, types, models, interfaces\n2. **Business logic**: services, utilities, core algorithms\n3. **Integration**: API endpoints, UI components, wiring\n4. **Quality**: tests, docs, manual verification checklists\n\nEach task should be buildable and testable in isolation once its dependencies are complete.\n\n#### Scope hygiene\n\n- **No refactoring beyond the task.** If the issue is \"add X\", don't pad it with \"also clean up Y\". File that as a separate issue.\n- **No speculative abstractions.** Don't introduce a helper/utility because it \"might be useful later.\" Add it when there is a concrete second caller.\n- **No silent scope expansion.** If you discover during analysis that fixing the issue properly requires changing something outside the obvious scope, flag it in Questions / Concerns \u2014 do not just silently expand the plan.\n\n---\n\n### Phase 4: Self-Review and Open Questions\n\nBefore committing to the plan, iterate internally once:\n\n1. **Completeness check** \u2014 does every acceptance criterion map to a task?\n2. **Dependency validation** \u2014 are tasks in the right order? Can each task be implemented with only the prior tasks complete?\n3. **Ambiguity detection** \u2014 list every unclear requirement, undefined behavior, or design decision that needs a human call.\n4. **Feasibility review** \u2014 is any single task too large (> ~1 commit of work)? Split it.\n5. **Pattern alignment** \u2014 does the plan follow the existing codebase conventions identified in Phase 2?\n\n#### Surface open questions\n\nFor each ambiguity, write a specific, actionable question. Vague questions are useless to the reviewer.\n\n**Good questions:**\n\n- \"Should the new authentication use JWT or session-based? The existing code in `src/modules/auth/` uses sessions, but the issue mentions 'stateless'.\"\n- \"The issue mentions 'caching' \u2014 in-memory, Redis, or file-based? No existing caching pattern in this repo to follow.\"\n- \"'Admin users' \u2014 is this a new role on the existing `User` model, or a separate `AdminUser` entity?\"\n\n**Bad questions:**\n\n- \"What should I do?\" \u2014 too vague\n- \"Is this OK?\" \u2014 not actionable\n- \"Should I follow best practices?\" \u2014 assumes no project context\n\nWhen multiple implementation approaches are viable, present them as options with trade-offs so the reviewer can choose:\n\n```\nOption A: Refactor existing component\n  + Cleaner architecture\n  + Less code duplication\n  - Higher risk, affects existing features\n  - Larger diff\n\nOption B: Create new component alongside\n  + Lower risk, isolated\n  + Easier to test\n  - Some duplication with existing component\n  - Two patterns coexist in the codebase\n```\n\n#### Interactive vs. programmatic mode\n\n- **Interactive:** ask the user your questions in chat, wait for answers, record the answers in the scratchpad's `Decisions Made` section, then regenerate any plan sections affected by the answers.\n- **Programmatic:** do NOT ask. Write every question into the scratchpad's `## Questions / Concerns \u2192 ### Clarifications Needed` section verbatim. Include the options/trade-offs so the reviewer can decide asynchronously. Document any assumptions you had to make under `### Assumptions Made` \u2014 each one should be labeled as an assumption so it can be challenged.\n\n---\n\n### Phase 5: Generate the Scratchpad\n\n#### Interactive mode\n\nWrite the following template to `SCRATCHPAD_{issue_number}.md` in the project root. Do NOT stage or commit it \u2014 the scratchpad is a working document that lives locally until `archive-work` runs.\n\n#### Programmatic mode\n\nDo NOT write to disk. Instead return the scratchpad content as a structured JSON envelope in your final assistant message. The caller supplies the envelope schema in the prompt (it typically includes fields for each section below: `summary`, `acceptance_criteria[]`, `implementation_tasks[]`, `affected_files[]`, `technical_notes`, `questions[]`, `assumptions[]`, `blockers[]`). The caller handles writing to the canonical plan path.\n\n#### Scratchpad template\n\n```markdown\n# {Issue Title} \u2014 #{issue_number}\n\n## Issue Details\n\n- **Repository:** {owner/repo}\n- **GitHub URL:** {issue_url}\n- **State:** {open/closed}\n- **Labels:** {comma-separated labels}\n- **Milestone:** {milestone title, or \"none\"}\n- **Assignees:** {names, or \"unassigned\"}\n- **Related Issues:**\n  - Depends on: {#N list, or \"none\"}\n  - Blocks: {#N list, or \"none\"}\n  - Related: {#N list, or \"none\"}\n\n## Description\n\n{Full issue body, verbatim}\n\n## Summary\n\n{One-paragraph restatement of what this plan proposes to do, in your own words. Explain the \"why\" in addition to the \"what\".}\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n{Parsed from the issue body's task list, or distilled from the description if no explicit task list.}\n\n- [ ] {criterion 1}\n- [ ] {criterion 2}\n\n## Branch Strategy\n\n- **Base branch:** {detected base \u2014 prefer develop-ts > develop > main}\n- **Feature branch:** {issue_number}-{slugified-title}\n- **Current branch:** {git branch --show-current}\n\n*(Programmatic mode: omit this section \u2014 the caller manages branches.)*\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### Setup\n\n- [ ] Fetch latest from base branch\n- [ ] Create and checkout feature branch\n\n### Implementation Tasks\n\n{Atomic, dependency-ordered tasks from Phase 3. Each task follows the anatomy: files, why, testing.}\n\n- [ ] {Task 1 title}\n  - **Files:** {paths}\n  - **Why:** {rationale + dependencies}\n  - **Testing:** {what to test}\n\n- [ ] {Task 2 title}\n  - **Files:** {paths}\n  - **Why:** {rationale + dependencies}\n  - **Testing:** {what to test}\n\n### Quality Checks\n\n- [ ] Run type checker / linter\n- [ ] Run relevant tests (unit + integration)\n- [ ] Self-review the diff for scope hygiene\n- [ ] Verify each acceptance criterion is met\n\n### Documentation\n\n- [ ] Update relevant README / docs if public behavior changed\n- [ ] Add inline comments only where logic is non-obvious\n\n## Affected Files\n\n{Concrete list of predicted files this plan will touch, with a one-line reason each. Approval refines the work item's predicted_files from this list.}\n\n- `path/to/file.ts` \u2014 {what changes}\n- `path/to/other.ts` \u2014 {what changes}\n\n## Technical Notes\n\n### Architecture Considerations\n\n{Architectural decisions to make, module boundaries to respect, integration points to handle. Reference specific file:line locations discovered in Phase 2.}\n\n### Implementation Approach\n\n{High-level strategy. If multiple approaches were considered, explain why this one was chosen.}\n\n### Potential Challenges\n\n{Known complexity, technical debt to navigate, performance considerations, edge cases.}\n\n## Questions / Concerns\n\n### Clarifications Needed\n\n{Open questions from Phase 4. In interactive mode these should already be resolved; in programmatic mode they stay here until the reviewer handles them.}\n\n- {Specific question with context and options}\n\n### Blocked By\n\n{Dependencies on other issues not yet complete. Reference by issue number.}\n\n- {#N \u2014 why this blocks}\n\n### Assumptions Made\n\n{Assumptions you had to make in the absence of clarification. Each one is a candidate to be challenged by the reviewer.}\n\n- {Assumption + what depends on it being correct}\n\n### Decisions Made\n\n{Populated during interactive Q&A. Format: Q \u2192 A (rationale). Empty in programmatic mode unless the caller supplies pre-resolved decisions.}\n\n## Work Log\n\n{Filled in during `do-work` \u2014 each work session adds a dated entry.}\n\n---\n\n**Generated:** {timestamp}\n**By:** setup-work skill\n**Source:** {github_issue_url}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Phase 6: Prepare Workspace (interactive mode only)\n\n**Skip this phase in programmatic mode** \u2014 the caller manages branches, and writing files is the caller's job.\n\n#### Detect base branch\n\n```bash\ngit fetch origin\n# Prefer in order: develop-ts \u2192 develop \u2192 main\ngit branch -r | grep -E 'origin/(develop-ts|develop|main)$' | head -1\n```\n\n#### Create feature branch\n\n```bash\ngit branch {issue_number}-{slugified-title} origin/{base_branch}\n```\n\nDo not check it out automatically \u2014 let the operator decide when to switch.\n\n#### Final output\n\nDisplay a concise summary:\n\n```\n\u2713 Issue #{number} analyzed and prepared\n\n\ud83d\udccb SCRATCHPAD_{number}.md created with:\n   - {N} implementation tasks\n   - {M} open questions  (or \"all questions resolved\")\n   - Affected files: {count}\n\n\ud83c\udf3f Branch '{branch_name}' created from {base_branch}\n\n\ud83d\udd17 GitHub Issue: {url}\n\n\ud83d\ude80 Next step: git checkout {branch_name}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Working Principles\n\n- **Depth over speed.** A rushed plan wastes far more time downstream than a careful one.\n- **Concrete over abstract.** Reference specific files, specific functions, specific line numbers. Avoid generic advice like \"add error handling where appropriate.\"\n- **Read-before-suggest.** Never propose modifications to a file you haven't actually read in this session.\n- **Atomic thinking.** Each task is a commit. Each commit tells one story. Each diff should be reviewable in under five minutes.\n- **Question assumptions.** If something is unclear, ask (interactive) or flag it (programmatic). Do not fill gaps with guesses and hope for the best.\n- **Context-aware.** Every project is different. Adapt the plan to the project's existing conventions rather than importing patterns from somewhere else.\n- **Scope discipline.** Do what the issue asks. Nothing more. Related improvements become new issues.\n\n---\n\n## Rules\n\n- Setup is **not complete** until the plan is approved (interactive: in chat; programmatic: via the caller's approval gate).\n- Surface every ambiguity. Don't assume.\n- If the issue body is vague, write the vagueness into `Clarifications Needed` rather than guessing.\n- If codebase analysis reveals complications (unexpected dependencies, deprecated patterns, cross-module refactors), flag them in `Potential Challenges` or `Clarifications Needed`.\n- The scratchpad is a reliable contract for what `do-work` will execute \u2014 invest the time to get it right.\n- **Never commit or push `SCRATCHPAD_*.md`** during setup. It stays untracked until `archive-work` moves it to the archive directory.\n- **Never modify unrelated files.** Setup is read-only except for the scratchpad itself.\n- In programmatic mode: return the structured envelope exactly as specified by the caller. No prose wrapper, no markdown fences around the JSON, no commentary before or after.\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\n### Issue not found\n\nVerify the issue number and repository. Confirm `gh` authentication is valid (`gh auth status`). If the issue is in a different repo than the current one, pass `--repo owner/repo` explicitly.\n\n### Insufficient issue information\n\nIf the issue body is sparse or ambiguous, do not guess. Note it prominently in `Clarifications Needed`. In interactive mode, consider suggesting the user add a task list to the issue before proceeding.\n\n### Branch already exists\n\nCheck for existing work (`git log {branch_name}`). If there are commits, this is probably a resume \u2014 delegate to `do-work` instead. If the branch is empty, warn and ask whether to delete and recreate.\n\n### Repository access issues\n\nVerify `gh auth status`. Check that the repo exists and the authenticated user has read access. For private repos, confirm the token has the right scope.\n\n### Tool failures (programmatic mode)\n\nIf a tool call fails irrecoverably, do not invent a scratchpad. Return an envelope with a clear `error` field so the caller can surface the failure and not transition work item state.\n\n---\n\n## Integration with other skills\n\n**Flows to:**\n- `do-work` \u2014 begins execution from the approved scratchpad\n- `commit-changes` \u2014 used during work loop, not during setup\n\n**Receives context from:**\n- The caller's project `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`\n- Optional programmatic prompt context from the caller\n\n---\n\n## Success Criteria\n\nA successful setup produces:\n\n- **Complete context:** all issue details captured verbatim\n- **Concrete plan:** atomic, dependency-ordered tasks with files + rationale\n- **Identified risks:** challenges flagged in Technical Notes\n- **Honest gaps:** unresolved questions surfaced, assumptions labeled as assumptions\n- **Ready workspace:** (interactive mode only) branch created from the right base\n\nThe scratchpad should be clear enough that another developer could pick it up and execute it without talking to you.\n"

`draft handles markdown-fenced JSON in the agent response` \u2014 mock returns ` ```json\\n{...}\\n``` `\n    - `draft throws on malformed JSON` \u2014 mock returns \"not json\", assert throw\n    - `draft throws when the envelope is missing required fields` \u2014 mock returns `{}`, assert throw mentions a missing field\n    - `draft throws when createAgentSession itself throws` \u2014 mock throws, drafter throws\n- **Why:** isolated tests for the drafter without needing PlansService context\n- **Testing:** `npx vitest run plan-drafter`\n\n#### Task 12: Quality gates + manual smoke\n\n- **Files:** none (verification only)\n- **What:**\n  - `npx tsc --noEmit`\n  - `npx vitest run`\n  - `npx vite build --config web/vite.config.ts`\n  - Restart dev server, click Prepare on a planned work item (e.g. studio-138), verify the scratchpad in the Review modal contains drafted content (not `(to be filled in)` placeholders), verify state transitioned to `drafting`. Click Prepare again, verify it re-drafted (content may differ).\n- **Why:** prove end-to-end before commits\n- **Testing:** see above\n\n### Quality Checks\n\n- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit`\n- [ ] `npx vitest run`\n- [ ] `npx vite build --config web/vite.config.ts`\n- [ ] Self-review the diff for scope hygiene (no unrelated changes, no speculative abstractions)\n- [ ] Verify each acceptance criterion is met\n- [ ] Manual smoke test on studio-138 in dev server\n\n### Documentation\n\n- [ ] No README updates expected \u2014 public behavior is \"Prepare button now produces real plans\" which is self-evident from the UI\n- [ ] No new ADR \u2014 this is a course-correction within ADR 014, not a new architectural decision\n- [ ] Inline JSDoc comments on `PlanDrafterService` methods explaining the prompt-building strategy\n\n## Affected Files\n\n- `package-lock.json` \u2014 bump escapement to ea6cdd1+\n- `src/modules/plans/types.ts` \u2014 add `PlanDraftEnvelope`, `PlanDraftTask`, `PlanDraftTechnicalNotes` interfaces\n- `src/modules/plans/plan-drafter.service.ts` \u2014 new service (resolves skill, builds prompt, calls createAgentSession, parses envelope)\n- `src/modules/plans/plans.module.ts` \u2014 register and export `PlanDrafterService`\n- `src/modules/plans/plans.service.ts` \u2014 `@Inject(PlanDrafterService)`, async prepare, drafter integration, extended `renderPlanScratchpad` signature, drop carry-forward branch\n- `src/modules/plans/plans.controller.ts` \u2014 async/await on prepare\n- `src/modules/plans/__tests__/plans.service.test.ts` \u2014 harness updated with drafter mock, tests rewritten for re-draft semantics\n- `src/modules/plans/__tests__/plan-drafter.service.test.ts` \u2014 new unit test file\n\n## Technical Notes\n\n### Architecture Considerations\n\n- **Single source of truth for the drafting spec.** The skill at `node_modules/escapement/skills/setup-work/SKILL.md` (sourced from the `escapement` GitHub dependency) is the canonical drafting instructions. PlansService reads it at runtime \u2014 no inline duplication, no `escapement-studio/docs/` copy. Bumping the dep is the only way to change drafter behavior, which is correct.\n- **DI gotcha avoidance.** Per the lesson learned in `e10632c` (the hotfix), every NestJS injection in this codebase needs explicit `@Inject(SomeService)` because tsx doesn't emit full decorator metadata. New `PlanDrafterService` consumers get explicit decorators.\n- **Async propagation.** `prepare` going async cascades through the controller (already done in #154 for other Plans endpoints? \u2014 verify) and any callers that test it synchronously. The test harness's `Object.create` pattern handles this naturally \u2014 tests just need `await`.\n- **Failure semantics.** Drafter throws \u2192 PlansService.prepare doesn't catch \u2192 NestJS converts to 500 \u2192 Studio UI shows error in the existing Prepare loading-state error path. No new error UI plumbing needed in #158's frontend.\n- **Drafter has full repo read access via `cwd: process.cwd()`.** This means the agent can Grep the actual escapement-studio source while drafting, which dramatically improves plan quality vs. issue-body-only drafting. For cross-repo work items (e.g. a work item for a different `repo` field), the agent still grep-reads escapement-studio \u2014 that's a known limitation noted in the issue's \"out of scope.\"\n\n### Implementation Approach\n\nMirrors `SubAgentService.runDelegation` (`src/modules/planning/sub-agent.service.ts:38-138`) very closely. Same imports, same `createAgentSession({ cwd, sessionManager, tools })` shape, same `await session.prompt() / session.dispose() / session.getLastAssistantText()` pattern, same JSON envelope parsing approach. The only meaningful differences:\n\n1. Tools list omits any write tools (we want read-only \u2014 Read + Grep + Bash, no Edit/Write)\n2. Prompt structure is different (skill body + work item + envelope schema, not focus paths + role + envelope schema)\n3. No artifact-dir bookkeeping (PlansService writes to the canonical scratchpad path, not a separate run dir)\n4. No \"recent runs\" buffer or metadata tracking \u2014 the drafter is stateless\n\nThe closest existing reference is SubAgentService \u2014 when in doubt, copy its pattern.\n\n### Potential Challenges\n\n- **Lockfile bump may pull in unrelated escapement changes.** The github: dep tracks main, so `npm install` will pull `ea6cdd1` AND any subsequent commits. If anything else has been pushed to escapement-pi main since `ea6cdd1`, those changes come along too. Mitigation: pin to exact SHA in package.json by changing `\"escapement\": \"github:fusupo/escapement-pi\"` \u2192 `\"escapement\": \"github:fusupo/escapement-pi#ea6cdd1\"`. **Decision needed**: do we want to pin? Argument for: reproducibility. Argument against: we lose automatic skill updates on the next deploy.\n  - **My take**: don't pin; track main. The whole point of the runtime-load architecture is to pick up future skill improvements. If a future skill change breaks Studio, that's a fast follow-up, not a reason to freeze.\n- **Skill prompt size.** The new skill is ~20KB / ~5K tokens. Plus the work item context, issue body, envelope schema, and the agent's tool-call exchanges. A typical drafting session could be 15-30K input tokens. At Sonnet 4 pricing (~$3/M input), each Prepare click costs roughly $0.05-0.10. For an interactive dev tool, that's fine.\n- **Latency.** Each Prepare click is a synchronous wait of 10-60s depending on how aggressive the agent is with tool calls. The Studio UI's `preparingPlan` state is the only feedback. If users complain, the next iteration is streaming (out of scope for #167).\n- **JSON parsing brittleness.** LLMs occasionally return JSON wrapped in markdown fences, with leading commentary, or with trailing commas. The `parseEnvelope` helper needs to handle the common variants. Don't try to be clever \u2014 strip fences if present, trim whitespace, JSON.parse, re-throw with context if it fails. Don't attempt JSON5 / yaml fallbacks; those create more problems than they solve.\n- **Test fragility around the harness pattern.** The existing tests use `Object.create(PlansService.prototype)` and manually inject properties. Adding a new injected dependency means updating the harness. Be careful to also inject `drafter` in every test that constructs a harness, otherwise existing tests will fail with \"drafter is undefined.\" A default mock drafter that returns a valid envelope avoids forcing every test to think about drafter behavior.\n- **Idempotency of re-prepare on drafting state.** Today the test `is idempotent on drafting \u2192 drafting and carries existing scratchpad forward` enforces a specific contract: if you re-prepare while drafting, your scratchpad isn't stomped. Removing this behavior changes the contract \u2014 anyone who manually edited a scratchpad will lose it on re-prepare. **This is intentional per the issue** (every Prepare re-drafts). If a user wanted to preserve manual edits, the right primitive is Approve (which transitions to ready and the plan is no longer re-prepareable). Document this in the test deletion commit message.\n\n## Questions / Concerns\n\n### Clarifications Needed\n\n(none \u2014 strategic decisions were resolved in the conversation that produced #167; tactical implementation details have clear precedents in SubAgentService)\n\n### Blocked By\n\n(none \u2014 fusupo/escapement-pi `ea6cdd1` is already pushed and the DI hotfix `e10632c` is already on develop)\n\n### Assumptions Made\n\n- **Drafter latency 10-60s is acceptable.** No timeout enforcement in the first cut. If the agent runs forever, the underlying pi-coding-agent session has its own implicit timeouts.\n- **The skill body fits in a single agent prompt.** ~5K tokens of skill + ~5K tokens of context. Well under Sonnet's context window.\n- **`process.cwd()` is the escapement-studio repo root** when the dev server runs. True today (verified \u2014 the `npm run dev` invocation runs from the repo root). If this ever changes, the drafter would silently grep the wrong codebase.\n- **The github: dep auto-resolves on `npm install`.** Confirmed \u2014 `escapement: \"github:fusupo/escapement-pi\"` re-fetches on `npm install` and the lockfile updates the resolved SHA. If this is wrong, we may need an explicit `npm update escapement` command.\n- **Drafter does NOT need to call `gh issue view`.** The issue body is fetched once by PlansService and passed as a prompt parameter. The drafter doesn't need its own GitHub access.\n\n### Decisions Made\n\n- **Always re-draft on every Prepare** (no carry-forward, no manual-edit detection) \u2014 confirmed in conversation: *\"redo the whole thing with each user action to 'prepare'\"*\n- **Fail loud on drafter errors** (no fallback to stub) \u2014 confirmed in conversation: *\"we should be straight\"*\n- **Refresh predicted_files from envelope.affected_files** \u2014 confirmed in conversation: *\"the drafter should refine/rewrite them\"*\n- **Use the bundled escapement skill, not an inlined copy** \u2014 confirmed in conversation: *\"why can't we basically use those prompts from ~/escapement-pi/skills? isn't escapement-pi already a dependency\"*\n- **Synchronous, not async with polling** \u2014 confirmed: *\"sync is fine\"*\n- **No separate scratchpad-planner pi agent** \u2014 content folded into the merged setup-work skill in `ea6cdd1`\n- **Don't pin escapement to SHA in package.json** \u2014 track main; assume future skill updates are wanted\n\n## Work Log\n\n(filled in during do-work)\n\n---\n\n**Generated:** 2026-04-09\n**By:** setup-work skill (Claude Code, applied to escapement-studio)\n**Source:** https://github.com/fusupo/escapement-studio/issues/167\n"
}

  "old_string": "  /**\n   * Draft (or re-draft) the canonical scratchpad for a work item and\n   * transition it to the `drafting` state. No worktree is created.\n   *\n   * - If the canonical scratchpad already exists and is non-empty, its\n   *   contents are carried forward unchanged (so in-progress plan edits are\n   *   not destroyed).\n   * - If it is absent or empty, a fresh skeleton is generated from the issue\n   *   body and Studio issue templates.\n   *\n   * Valid pre-states: `planned`, `drafting`. Everything else throws\n   * `BadRequestException`.\n   */\n  prepare(workItemId: string): PlanResponse {\n    const workItem = this.workItemsService.get(workItemId);\n    this.assertPreparable(workItem);\n\n    // Transition work item state FIRST so concurrent prepare requests for\n    // the same work item fail fast on the state guard (they will observe\n    // `drafting`, not `planned`, if they lose the race). The state guard\n    // allows drafting \u2192 drafting (re-prepare) but rejects everything else.\n    const transitioned =\n      workItem.state === \"drafting\"\n        ? workItem\n        : this.workItemsService.update(workItemId, { state: \"drafting\" });\n\n    // Ensure the plan dir exists and write initial metadata if we were first.\n    ensurePlanDir(this.artifactRoot, workItemId);\n\n    const canonicalPath = canonicalScratchpadPath(this.artifactRoot, workItemId);\n    let scratchpadContent: string;\n    if (existsSync(canonicalPath)) {\n      const existing = readFileSync(canonicalPath, \"utf8\");\n      if (existing.trim().length > 0) {\n        scratchpadContent = existing;\n      } else {\n        scratchpadContent = this.generateSkeleton(transitioned);\n        writeFileSync(canonicalPath, scratchpadContent, \"utf8\");\n      }\n    } else {\n      scratchpadContent = this.generateSkeleton(transitioned);\n      writeFileSync(canonicalPath, scratchpadContent, \"utf8\");\n    }\n\n    // Update plan metadata to reflect drafting state.\n    const metadata = this.updatePlanMetadata(workItemId, (current) => ({\n      ...current,\n      state: \"drafting\",\n      scratchpad_path: canonicalPath,\n    }));\n\n    return {\n      work_item_id: workItemId,\n      metadata,\n      scratchpad_content: scratchpadContent,\n    };\n  }",
  "new_string": "  /**\n   * Draft (or re-draft) the canonical scratchpad for a work item and\n   * transition it to the `drafting` state. No worktree is created.\n   *\n   * Per ADR 014 step 8 follow-up (#167), every call invokes\n   * `PlanDrafterService.draft()` to produce a fresh `PlanDraftEnvelope` from\n   * a one-shot pi-coding-agent session. The envelope is injected into the\n   * canonical scratchpad and the work item's `predicted_files` is refreshed\n   * from the envelope's `affected_files`.\n   *\n   * **Always re-drafts.** Re-running prepare on a work item already in\n   * `drafting` state runs the drafter again from scratch \u2014 no carry-forward\n   * of prior content. If you want to preserve manual edits, hit Approve\n   * (which transitions to `ready`) before re-clicking Prepare.\n   *\n   * **Fails loud.** If the drafter throws (network error, malformed JSON,\n   * agent failure), the exception propagates and the work item state does\n   * NOT transition. The existing scratchpad and metadata are not modified.\n   *\n   * Valid pre-states: `planned`, `drafting`. Everything else throws\n   * `BadRequestException`.\n   */\n  async prepare(workItemId: string): Promise<PlanResponse> {\n    const workItem = this.workItemsService.get(workItemId);\n    this.assertPreparable(workItem);\n\n    // Fetch the issue body once and pass it into both the drafter and the\n    // renderer. The drafter doesn't need its own gh access.\n    const issueBody = fetchIssueBody(workItem.repo, workItem.issue_number);\n\n    // Run the drafter BEFORE any state mutation. If this throws, no state\n    // changes are visible and the caller can retry.\n    const draft = await this.drafter.draft(workItem, issueBody);\n\n    // Drafter succeeded. From here on, all mutations land.\n\n    // Refresh the work item's predicted_files from the drafter's\n    // affected_files. Skip if the drafter returned an empty list (preserve\n    // the current value rather than nuking it).\n    if (draft.affected_files.length > 0) {\n      this.workItemsService.update(workItemId, {\n        predicted_files: draft.affected_files,\n      });\n    }\n\n    // Transition work item state if not already drafting (prepare is\n    // idempotent on the state transition itself; it just re-runs the drafter\n    // and overwrites the scratchpad).\n    if (workItem.state !== \"drafting\") {\n      this.workItemsService.update(workItemId, { state: \"drafting\" });\n    }\n\n    // Ensure the plan dir exists and write initial metadata if we were first.\n    ensurePlanDir(this.artifactRoot, workItemId);\n\n    // Render and overwrite the canonical scratchpad with the drafted content.\n    // We re-fetch the (possibly updated) work item so the renderer sees the\n    // refreshed predicted_files.\n    const refreshed = this.workItemsService.get(workItemId);\n    const templates = this.templateService.listTemplates();\n    const scratchpadContent = this.renderPlanScratchpad(\n      refreshed,\n      issueBody,\n      templates,\n      draft,\n    );\n    const canonicalPath = canonicalScratchpadPath(this.artifactRoot, workItemId);\n    writeFileSync(canonicalPath, scratchpadContent, \"utf8\");\n\n    // Update plan metadata to reflect drafting state.\n    const metadata = this.updatePlanMetadata(workItemId, (current) => ({\n      ...current,\n      state: \"drafting\",\n      scratchpad_path: canonicalPath,\n    }));\n\n    return {\n      work_item_id: workItemId,\n      metadata,\n      scratchpad_content: scratchpadContent,\n    };\n  }"
}

Real-LLM smoke caught a parser fragility. The agent did the work correctly (3:17 minute session, ran tools, drafted real JSON) but **prefixed the response with a sentence** before the JSON object, despite the prompt's "no commentary" instruction:

```
Now I have enough to draft the plan. Producing the JSON envelope.

{
  "summary": "..."
```

Models occasionally do this even with strict instructions. The right fix is to make the parser **more lenient** — extract the first balanced JSON object from anywhere in the response, rather than requiring the whole text to be valid JSON. The agent's actual output is fine; only my parser is too strict.
